skill.name: teardown
skill.description: Build an interactive 3D simulator of a real machine or mechanism (an engine, a landing gear, a walking linkage, a pump, a gearbox) as one offline HTML page people can take apart, with live panels driven by the same model that moves the parts, a button for every subsystem, cutaways, camera views and an auto tour that hands control to the visitor; then record it frame by frame to a 60 fps video with a synced procedural score. Use when someone asks how a machine works, wants a "visual explainer", a "simulator", a "cutaway", an "exploded view" or an "interactive 3D lesson", or wants a 3D object shown working rather than described.
skill.summary: Create offline interactive machine simulators with synchronized controls, cutaways, frame capture, and procedural sound.
skill.author: elvarofficial

remediation.suggestion: Reject path separators and parent segments in --name. Verify resolved paths remain inside the output folder, and avoid deleting existing directories recursively.

high_findings.title: innerHTML assignment (XSS risk)
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: runtime.js merges URL-supplied story configuration into captions. Unescaped tag, text, and kind values reach innerHTML, allowing scripts through injected HTML event handlers.

high_findings.title: Node.js fs operations
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The unchecked --name value reaches recursive, forced deletion through path.join(base, name). Parent segments can delete directories outside the sheet output folder.

medium_findings.title: Node.js fs operations
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The unchecked --name also controls this directory and subsequent frame writes. Parent segments permit output creation outside the intended sheet folder.

content.value_statement: Static diagrams make moving mechanisms difficult to understand. Teardown combines interactive 3D models, synchronized readouts, and recorded tours in a reusable production workflow.
actual_capabilities: Bundle simulator code, fonts, and styles into offline HTML pages with optional external model assets.
Provide V8 engine, Cessna landing gear, and Jansen linkage examples with live and film variants.
Connect mechanism motion to numeric readouts, charts, camera views, and cutaway controls.
Capture deterministic frames, individual stills, review sheets, and MP4 video through Chromium and FFmpeg.
Generate timeline-synchronized procedural audio and master stereo WAV output with loudness and peak controls.
Create waveform images and review sheets from rendered media for visual and audio checks.
limitations: New machines require reference material, dimensions, and custom modeling code; arbitrary mechanisms are not generated automatically.
Setup requires Node.js dependencies and Chromium; video and audio workflows also require FFmpeg and Python.
GPU performance varies, and the examples use a fixed 1600 by 900 overlay scaled to fit the viewport.
Caption rendering and contact-sheet path handling have unresolved security risks; recorded-sample decoding also uses a hardcoded Windows FFmpeg path.

use_cases.title: Explain Mechanisms in Class
use_cases.description: Adapt a bundled machine to let students inspect motion, cutaways, and matching numeric readouts in an offline browser page.

use_cases.title: Produce Technical Demonstration Videos
use_cases.description: Record a deterministic mechanism tour, generate synchronized sound, and inspect review sheets before exporting a demonstration video.

use_cases.title: Prototype Interactive Product Explanations
use_cases.description: Use reference dimensions to build an interactive mechanism model with subsystem controls and coordinated charts for stakeholder review.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Bundled Example
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the bundled V8 live example as offline HTML. Report the output location and any missing dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Customize a Mechanism Lesson
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the bundled landing gear example for a classroom lesson. Keep readouts linked to actuator stroke and preserve camera and cutaway controls.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Reference-Based Machine
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an offline simulator of [mechanism] using [references] and [dimensions]. Separate kinematics, geometry, controls, and rendering; identify missing measurements before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Produce and Review a Recorded Tour
prompt_templates.prompt: Record [simulator] at 60 fps with synchronized procedural audio. Generate timeline review sheets, inspect every tile, and report measured loudness and unresolved defects.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: complete the capture and review workflow.

output_examples.input: Build the bundled V8 engine as an offline interactive lesson.
output: Deliverable: an offline HTML engine explorer with cylinder selection, cutaway modes, camera views, and crank-linked charts.
Review focus: compare piston motion, firing order, and valve timing against the displayed mechanism state.

output_examples.input: Prepare a recorded landing gear explanation with synchronized audio and review material.
output: Deliverables: a frame-captured MP4 tour, a procedural WAV score, and contact sheets covering timeline beats.
Review focus: inspect gear clearance, annotation placement, transition timing, and the final encoded audio levels.

best_practices: Start with real references and dimensions, then derive motion and displayed values from one shared mechanism model.
Keep frame rendering deterministic and use the same timeline for camera actions, review frames, and audio events.
Review generated frame sheets and final media, test integrated GPU performance, and use trusted configurations until security issues are fixed.
anti_patterns: Inventing mechanism dimensions or animating gauges independently from the geometry.
Using nondeterministic frame updates and assuming live playback will match captured output.
Accepting untrusted caption configuration or path-like contact-sheet names before the reported security issues are fixed.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that can edit files and run local commands.

faq.question: Can the generated simulator run offline?
faq.answer: Default builds inline scripts, fonts, and styles. Builds with external model assets need those files alongside the HTML page.

faq.question: Which mechanisms are included?
faq.answer: The examples cover a cross-plane V8 engine, Cessna 337 main landing gear, and a Theo Jansen walking linkage.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: Building needs Node.js dependencies. Capture needs Chromium and FFmpeg; procedural scoring needs Python. The recorded-sample decoder currently contains a Windows-specific FFmpeg path.

faq.question: Does this replace engineering validation?
faq.answer: No. These are educational visualizations with authored models. Verify dimensions, assumptions, and results against reliable engineering references.

faq.question: Are there security restrictions?
faq.answer: Use trusted configuration and simple sheet names. Caption HTML injection and unsafe directory deletion remain unresolved, and omitted static matches still need review.
